caption: Container
description: The Container object describes an instance of a specific container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.
name: container

hash.description: Commit hash of image created for docker or the SHA256 hash of the container. For example: 13550340a8681c84c861aac2e5b440161c2b33a3e4f302ac680ca5b686de48de.

image.description: The container image used as a template to run the container.

is_host_ipc.description: Indicates that the container shares the IPC namespace of the host, so it can use the host's shared memory and other IPC objects. For example, the Kubernetes pod setting hostIPC: true, or an IPC mode of host in the container runtime.

references.description: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards, Baseline policy, Host Namespaces
Docker Engine API, container create and inspect, HostConfig

is_host_network.description: Indicates that the container shares the network namespace of the host, so it sees and uses the host's network interfaces and can bind to its ports and reach services listening on its loopback address. For example, the Kubernetes pod setting hostNetwork: true, or a network mode of host in the container runtime.

references.description: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards, Baseline policy, Host Namespaces
Docker Engine API, container create and inspect, HostConfig

is_host_pid.description: Indicates that the container shares the PID namespace of the host, so it can see, and with enough privileges signal or trace, every process on the host. For example, the Kubernetes pod setting hostPID: true, or a PID mode of host in the container runtime.

references.description: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards, Baseline policy, Host Namespaces
Docker Engine API, container create and inspect, HostConfig

is_privileged.description: Indicates that the container runs in privileged mode. A privileged container gets all kernel capabilities and access to the host devices, and the runtime does not apply its default system call filter, AppArmor or SELinux confinement, so it is not isolated from the host in a meaningful way.

references.description: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards, Baseline policy, Privileged Containers

labels.description: The list of labels associated to the container.

size.description: The size of the container image.

tag.description: The tag used by the container. It can indicate version, format, OS.

tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the container.

uid.description: The full container unique identifier for this instantiation of the container. For example: ac2ea168264a08f9aaca0dfc82ff3551418dfd22d02b713142a6843caa2f61bf.
